Referenced GLib error type used as an out-parameter in gst_init_check(). It is not defined in this header. Note: this is a pointer-to-pointer, reflecting typical GLib error reporting conventions.

functions.name: gst_init
functions.description: Initializes the GStreamer library and processes/strips any GStreamer-related command-line arguments from the application's argv. Must be called before most other GStreamer API is used.
requirements: Should be called once early in program startup, before creating or using GStreamer objects.
argc must point to an integer variable representing the argument count; argv must point to the argument vector as declared; both should be valid writable pointers if argument processing is desired.
It is common for init-style functions to accept NULL for argc/argv to skip argument parsing, but this header does not state that explicitly; clarify if NULL is permitted before relying on it.
Not thread-safe to call concurrently; call during single-threaded initialization.

functions.name: gst_init_check
functions.description: Initializes GStreamer like gst_init but returns a gboolean indicating success and reports initialization errors via a GError. Useful when initialization may fail and the application needs to handle that gracefully.
requirements: Call early, before other GStreamer API usage.
argc and argv must be valid pointers if argument processing is required; types must match the signature.
error may be NULL to ignore details; otherwise follow GLib convention: pass the address of a GError* initialized to NULL; the function may set it on failure.
Check the return value: TRUE on success, FALSE on failure; on FALSE, do not use GStreamer APIs that require initialization.
Not safe to call concurrently from multiple threads; perform during single-threaded startup.

functions.name: gst_is_initialized
functions.description: Returns whether the GStreamer library has been successfully initialized in this process.
requirements: No preconditions; can be called at any time.
Use the return value to guard calls that require prior initialization.

functions.name: gst_init_get_option_group
functions.description: Returns a GOptionGroup for GStreamer's command-line options to integrate into a GLib GOptionContext. Allows applications to merge GStreamer option handling with their own.
requirements: Intended for use with GLib's GOptionContext; the caller should add the returned group to a GOptionContext before parsing.
Ownership/lifetime rules are not stated here; typical GLib pattern is that the returned group is owned by the caller or by GStreamer depending on docs—clarify before freeing.
Should be used before parsing command-line options.

functions.name: gst_deinit
functions.description: Deinitializes the GStreamer library, releasing global resources allocated during initialization. Rarely needed in typical applications.
requirements: Call only after successful initialization and after application is done using GStreamer objects.
Do not use GStreamer APIs that require initialization after calling this.
Not thread-safe with concurrent GStreamer use; ensure no other threads are using GStreamer when deinitializing.

functions.name: gst_version
functions.description: Retrieves the compile-time/runtime GStreamer version components via output parameters.
requirements: Provide writable pointers for any components you want to retrieve; unknown from this header whether NULL is allowed to skip fields—clarify before passing NULL.
Pointers provided, if non-NULL, must be valid and writable.
No initialization required; safe to call at any time.

functions.name: gst_version_string
functions.description: Returns a newly-allocated human-readable string describing the GStreamer version.
requirements: The returned string is dynamically allocated per GLib/GStreamer conventions and should be freed by the caller, typically with g_free().
Return value may be NULL on allocation failure (not specified here); handle defensively.

functions.name: gst_check_version
functions.signature: gboolean gst_check_version (guint major, guint minor, guint micro);
functions.description: Checks whether the GStreamer library version is at least the specified major.minor.micro. Returns TRUE if the requirement is met.
requirements: major, minor, and micro should specify a non-negative version triple.
Use the return value to gate use of APIs that require a minimum GStreamer version.

functions.name: gst_segtrap_is_enabled
functions.description: Queries whether GStreamer's segmentation-fault trapping mechanism is enabled. When enabled, GStreamer may install handlers to aid debugging crashes.
requirements: No preconditions; callable at any time.
Use only for diagnostic/configuration logic; behavior specifics are not detailed here.

functions.name: gst_segtrap_set_enabled
functions.description: Enables or disables GStreamer's segmentation-fault trapping mechanism.
requirements: Call early in program startup to ensure handlers are set before other threads/components initialize.
enabled must be a valid gboolean (0/1).
Be aware that changing trap settings affects process-wide signal handling; coordinate with other crash/handler frameworks.

functions.name: gst_registry_fork_is_enabled
functions.description: Returns whether the registry scanning via a helper subprocess (registry fork) is enabled. This affects how plugin registries are discovered/updated.
requirements: No preconditions; callable at any time.
Use to decide how registry updates will be performed.

functions.name: gst_registry_fork_set_enabled
functions.description: Enables or disables the use of a helper subprocess to scan/update the plugin registry.
requirements: Call before triggering registry updates to ensure the desired behavior.
enabled must be a valid gboolean (0/1).
Affects process-wide registry behavior; ensure consistency across the application.

functions.name: gst_update_registry
functions.description: Forces an update of the GStreamer plugin registry, scanning available plugins and writing out the registry cache. Returns TRUE on success.
requirements: Should not be called concurrently from multiple threads; perform when no other thread is loading plugins.
Check return value for success before assuming the registry is updated.
May be an expensive operation; use sparingly.

functions.name: gst_get_main_executable_path
functions.description: Returns the filesystem path to the program’s main executable as a constant string, if available.
requirements: Return value must not be modified by the caller.
Lifetime/ownership are not specified here; treat as borrowed; copy the string if you need to keep it beyond immediate use.
May return NULL if the path cannot be determined; handle that case.

data_types.description: A generic command-line argument token as a UTF-8 or byte string, suitable for inclusion in argv when parsing program options. May contain typical option forms (e.g., "-v", "--flag", "--key=value"), positional arguments, or arbitrary bytes. No specific encoding or structure is required beyond being a null-terminated C string; consumers may parse it according to standard CLI conventions.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
import itertools

# Generator for valid command-line argument vectors serialized into a single buffer.
# The fuzz stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR repeatedly to populate argv entries (<=64 bytes each),
# and also pull an unsigned int for argc. We will encode both the argc selector and a
# sequence of interesting argv strings so the harness can read them deterministically.
#
# Buffer format (little-endian):
#   [4 bytes] argc_hint (0..5 recommended by stub)
#   Then a sequence of N entries, each as:
#       [1 byte] length L (0..63)
#       [L bytes] UTF-8/bytes content (no NULs inside; stub adds NUL terminator)
#   We provide between 0 and 5 entries to match the stub's maximum.
# The FUZZ framework will likely sample the buffer in order for FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
# and FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls, so arranging argc first and then strings increases chance
# of consistent use. We include a variety of typical CLI patterns to exercise GStreamer
# option parsing: flags, key=value, with/without dashes, environment-like paths, etc.

CLI_TOKENS_BASE = [
    "app",  # argv[0] typical program name
    "-v",
    "-vv",
    "--verbose",
    "--quiet",
    "--gst-debug=*:3",
    "--gst-debug-level=5",
    "--gst-plugin-path=/tmp/plugins",
    "--gst-plugin-scan-stats",
    "--gst-disable-registry-fork",
    "--gst-enable-registry-fork",
    "--gst-debug-no-color",
    "--gst-plugin-load=fakeplugin",
    "--help",
    "--version",
    "-h",
    "--",
    "file:///tmp/input.avi",
    "input.mp4",
    "-o",
    "output.ts",
    "--key=value",
    "--flag",
    "positional",
]

# Additional variability including Unicode and edge cases but valid within 63 bytes
UNICODE_TOKENS = [
    "Vídeo",
    "路径/文件.mp4",
    "–dash",  # en dash to see UTF-8 handling
    "список",
]

PATH_TOKENS = [
    "/usr/bin/gst-launch-1.0",
    "/etc/gstreamer/1.0/plugins.conf",
    "C:/Program Files/GStreamer/bin/gst-launch-1.0.exe",
]

EQUAL_STYLE = [
    "--option=",
    "--opt=123",
    "--long-opt=value-with-dashes",
]

# Ensure max 63 chars per stub restriction. Truncate if necessary.

def clamp_token(s: str) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    if len(b) > 63:
        b = b[:63]
    return b


def synthesize_tokens(rng: random.Random, target_count: int) -> list[bytes]:
    # Build a pool and sample without exceeding 63 bytes per token.
    pool = [
        *CLI_TOKENS_BASE,
        *UNICODE_TOKENS,
        *PATH_TOKENS,
        *EQUAL_STYLE,
    ]
    # Create some combined patterns like --key=value and positional pairs
    extra = []
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        k = rng.choice(["--gst-debug", "--gst-plugin-load", "--name", "--caps"]) \
            + "=" + rng.choice(["*", "videoconvert:3", "fake", "audio/x-raw"]) 
        extra.append(k)
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        extra.append("-f")
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        extra.append("--no-color")
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        extra.append("--gst-fatal-warnings")
    pool.extend(extra)

    # Ensure argv[0] looks like an executable name sometimes
    argv0_choices = ["app", "gst-launch-1.0", "myprog", "test"]

    tokens: list[bytes] = []
    if target_count > 0:
        tokens.append(clamp_token(rng.choice(argv0_choices)))
    # Fill the rest
    while len(tokens) < target_count:
        # Occasionally generate a random-looking token within size limit
        if rng.random() < 0.35:
            length = rng.randint(0, 63)
            # Prefer printable but allow some bytes
            alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-._/:=,*+[]{}@\"'"
            b = bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
            tokens.append(b)
        else:
            s = rng.choice(pool)
            tokens.append(clamp_token(s))
    return tokens


def encode_argv(argc_hint: int, tokens: list[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Serialize argc first, then L+data entries for each token
    out = bytearray()
    out += struct.pack('<I', argc_hint & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    for tok in tokens:
        L = len(tok)
        if L > 63:
            L = 63
            tok = tok[:63]
        out.append(L)
        out += tok
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # The stub modulos argc to 0..5; we choose a value in that range, with bias toward small lists
    argc_hint = rng.choices([0,1,2,3,4,5], weights=[1,3,4,3,2,1])[0]
    count = argc_hint
    # Create tokens matching count; if count is 0, we still serialize only argc (no entries)
    tokens = synthesize_tokens(rng, count)

    buf = encode_argv(argc_hint, tokens)
    # Ensure total size <= 4096 (it will be small)
    return buf
